title: Float
body:
`float`. A real number in 4 bytes, about 7 significant digits. Half the size of a
[[Double]] and half the precision. An [[Atomic type]].

Use `double` unless you have a reason not to. `float` exists for when you have millions of
values and the memory matters, which is not this course. A bare literal like `3.14` is a
`double`; `3.14f` is a `float`.

Same approximation caveats as [[Double]], only sooner.
